title: The Best Marathons and Half Marathons in Vietnam
seo_title: Best Marathons and Half Marathons in Vietnam, From Results Data
meta_description: Vietnam's marathon fields are Southeast Asia's fastest. Official results compared, with field sizes, finish times and fees, and picks from Ha Long, Hanoi, Hue and Ho Chi Minh City.
dek: In Run SEA's results data, Vietnam's marathons are the fastest in Southeast Asia: every Vietnamese marathon we hold beats the regional median by more than half an hour. Here is what the results show, when to go, and which races to pick.

sections.heading: The Fastest Marathon Fields in the Region
paragraphs: Run SEA holds official results for nine Vietnamese races, about 67,000 finishers across editions from 2022 to 2026 [1]. Four of them held marathons in 2026: the VPBank Hanoi International Marathon, the Hue Amazing Marathon, the Techcombank Hanoi International Marathon and the VPBank Dat Sen Hong Music Marathon in Dong Thap. Their medians ran from 4:35 to 4:50, and 23% to 28% of finishers broke four hours [1].

Across all 25 Southeast Asian marathons in our 2026 data, the median finish is 5:25 and 11% of finishers break four hours [2]. Those four Vietnamese races have the four fastest medians of the 25. Pooled, their 4,721 finishers had a median of 4:41, and 25.8% went under four hours [1][2].

The fastest field we hold is the 2025 Halong Bay Heritage Marathon: 2,579 marathon finishers, a 4:08 median, and 45.8% under four hours [1]. The fastest quarter of its field had all finished by 3:43 [1].

Part of the gap comes from cut-offs. The last finishers at Vietnamese marathons come in at around six and a half hours, against seven to nine hours at most other races in the region, so the slow tail is shorter [1][2]. But the front of the field is faster too. At VPBank Hanoi the fastest quarter of finishers had all crossed the line by 3:57, and at Techcombank Hanoi by about 4:00. At the Singapore marathon the same mark was about 4:31, and at the Manila Marathon about 5:13 [1][2].

sections.heading: Half Marathons, Women and Fees
paragraphs: Half marathons are fast too. Eight Vietnamese half marathons from 2026, with 16,464 finishers between them, had a pooled median of 2:29, and 20.2% broke two hours. Across 74 half marathons region-wide the figures are 2:42 and 12% [1][2]. Not every Vietnamese half is part of a marathon weekend: 19 of the 39 Vietnamese race editions on our calendar go no longer than the half [3].

Women made up 18% of Vietnamese marathon finishers, level with the regional share. They made up 25% of half-marathon finishers, below the regional 29% [1][2]. The 2025 Halong Bay half was the exception, at 35% [1].

Of the 39 race editions, 25 list a fee range. The typical range runs from about VND 400,000 for the shortest distance to VND 960,000 for the longest, and events with a marathon have a median top fee of about VND 1.14 million [3]. The big Hanoi races cost more: VPBank Hanoi listed VND 1,668,000 for its standard-phase marathon entry, and the Standard Chartered Hanoi Marathon Heritage Race's adult fees ran up to VND 2,000,000 in 2025 [3].

sections.heading: When to Race: October to December
paragraphs: Of those 39 race editions, 28 (72%) fall between October and December, and November is the busiest month, with 13 races [3]. January adds five more. The calendar has nothing from May to July or in September, and a short August cluster (Hue, Nha Trang and a Ho Chi Minh City half marathon) opens the season [3].
The upcoming Vietnamese marathons and half marathons listed below this article update from the Run SEA calendar, so dates and fees there are current.

sections.heading: Ha Long: The Fast, Scenic Pick
paragraphs: The Halong Bay Heritage Marathon, organised by DHA Vietnam, marked its tenth anniversary in 2025. It grew from just over 400 runners at its first edition to about 14,000 athletes, around 3,000 of them from abroad [4]. The 2025 race set a men's course record of 2:13:57, and it was described as the only event in Vietnam holding a World Athletics Label Road Race designation [5]. The course follows the Tran Quoc Nghien coast road [5].

Its results justify the trip: the fastest marathon field in our data, and a 3,424-finisher half marathon with a 2:20 median, 26% under two hours and 35% women [1]. The 2026 edition is at runsea.run/race/halong-bay-heritage-marathon-2026/. For a quick half earlier in the autumn, DHA Vietnam's Global Gate Halong ESG Marathon, a half marathon and shorter races, had a 2:17 median in October 2026, with 32% of its 1,742 finishers under two hours [1].

sections.heading: Hanoi: Four Marathons in Two Months
paragraphs: Hanoi has the deepest choice, with four marathons between early October and late November [3]. The Techcombank Hanoi International Marathon, in early October, has grown quickly: its marathon field went from 1,110 finishers in 2024 to 1,967 in 2025 and 1,975 in 2026, and its half from 2,587 to 4,425 [1]. The 2026 marathon median was 4:43 [1].

The VPBank Hanoi International Marathon follows in mid-October. Its 2025 edition was its sixth, with about 11,000 athletes. Runners start from the Hoan Kiem Lake area, the marathon route passes four lakes and three bridges, and all four distances are AIMS-certified [6]. Its 2026 marathon had the fastest median of any Southeast Asian marathon that year, 4:35 [1][2].

The Standard Chartered Hanoi Marathon Heritage Race, in early November, has the longest history of the four. It began in 2018 as the Hanoi International Heritage Marathon and ran as the VPBank Hanoi Marathon from 2019. It reverted to the Hanoi Marathon Heritage Race name in 2023 and took Standard Chartered as title sponsor in 2024 [7][8]. DHA Vietnam organises it, and its routes are standardised by experts from the Vietnam Athletics Federation and AIMS [8]. It is a different race from the VPBank Hanoi International Marathon.
The fourth, the VnExpress Marathon Hanoi Midnight at the end of November, is a night race: in 2025 its marathon started at 12.05am, from Quang Trung street by Thien Quang Lake [3].

sections.heading: Hue, Dong Thap and Ho Chi Minh City
paragraphs: The Hue Amazing Marathon, at the end of August, starts beside the Flag Tower of the old citadel [3]. Its 2026 marathon was small but fast: 350 finishers, a 4:39 median and 26% under four hours [1]. The VPBank Dat Sen Hong Music Marathon in Cao Lanh, Dong Thap, shows how quickly provincial races are growing. It had 133 marathon finishers in 2022 and 552 in 2026, and its half grew from 715 to 2,630 [1].

Ho Chi Minh City's flagship is the Techcombank Ho Chi Minh City International Marathon in December. Organised by Sunrise Events Vietnam, its 2025 edition, the eighth, drew more than 23,000 runners from 81 countries and territories [9]. Run SEA does not yet hold its results. For a city half marathon in the south, Garmin Run Vietnam (2,941 half-marathon finishers in 2026, a 2:25 median) and the Gemadept Run (685, also 2:25) are the bigger fields in our data [1].

faqs.question: Are Vietnam's marathons really faster than the rest of Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: Yes, in Run SEA's results data. The four Vietnamese marathons we hold for 2026 had medians of 4:35 to 4:50, the four fastest of 25 Southeast Asian marathons, against a regional median of 5:25. Tighter cut-offs explain part of the gap, but the fastest quarter of Vietnamese fields also finishes about half an hour ahead of Singapore's.

faqs.question: Which Vietnamese marathon is best for a fast time?
faqs.answer: The Halong Bay Heritage Marathon. Its 2025 edition had the fastest field Run SEA holds: 2,579 marathon finishers with a 4:08 median, and 45.8% under four hours. It runs in late November on the coast road at Ha Long. Among the Hanoi races, VPBank Hanoi had the fastest 2026 median, at 4:35.

faqs.question: When is marathon season in Vietnam?
faqs.answer: October to December. Of the 39 Vietnamese race editions on the Run SEA calendar, 28 fall in those three months, and November is the busiest, with 13 races. Hanoi's four marathons run between early October and late November, and Ho Chi Minh City's flagship marathon follows in December.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 6 Nov 2026 from Run SEA's own results and calendar data, absorbing the best-full-marathon-races-in-vietnam and best-half-marathon-races-in-vietnam lists. Audit figures verified: 2026 Vietnamese marathon medians 4:35:08 (VPBank Hanoi), 4:38:48 (Hue), 4:42:33 (Techcombank Hanoi), 4:50:05 (VPBank Dat Sen Hong); sub-4 shares 27.6%, 26.3%, 24.9%, 23.2%. Halong Bay Heritage 2025 (data/finish-times-history): 2,579 finishers, median 4:08:12, 45.8% sub-4. Cut-off caveat checked: last finishers 6:26 to 6:51 in Vietnam vs 7:06 to 9:01 elsewhere; 25th-percentile times 3:43 to 4:06 in Vietnam vs 4:30 (Singapore), 4:44 (Maybank), 5:12 (Manila). The lists' 'IAAF- and AIMS-certified with a verified track record back to 2018' claim for the Hanoi Heritage Race is dropped: the race did start in 2018, but the IAAF/AIMS certificates Wikipedia records date from 2019, and the race has changed name and sponsor since (VPBank 2019-2022, Standard Chartered from 2024). Only the Halong label is named, as reported by Viet Nam News in Nov 2025; the current World Athletics label calendar page could not be read. The 'Vietnam has no standalone half marathons' line in the old list was wrong (19 of 39 editions top out at the half) and is corrected. Ha Long Bay's UNESCO listing is not repeated because the UNESCO page returned 403 today. Fees as listed in data/entities, which vary by entry phase. External sources checked 2026-11-06. Earlier 'scores' (88/100) dropped.
